data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004's causal mechanism is that 'Architectural Distance' (heterogeneous stacks) prevents propagation of systemic software bugs, making decentralization more resilient than a large service with strictly more internal redundancy. This mechanism is incomplete as a causal claim because it fails to account for correlated failure from shared upstream dependencies: it lists a common DNS provider as a countercondition, but the mechanism does not explain how architectural distance provides any resilience advantage against exactly the class of correlated failures the problem asks about. A large internally redundant service can also use heterogeneous stacks across its redundant nodes, so 'Architectural Distance' is not a property unique to decentralization and cannot causally explain why the decentralized network is more resilient.
